title: THE EFFECTIVENESS OF CHATGPT IN ENHANCING ACADEMIC WRITING SKILLS OF GRADE 11 STUDENTS
venue: European Journal of Foreign Language Teaching
extended_summary:
This paper investigates whether ChatGPT can improve the academic writing skills of senior high school students. The problem motivating the study is that Grade 11 students were reportedly struggling with core writing skills such as sentence construction, grammar, coherence, organization, and academic expression. The study frames this as an instructional need within English for Academic and Professional Purposes and related writing-intensive subjects, and positions AI-assisted writing support as a possible intervention.

The intervention consisted of a 14-day ChatGPT-supported writing program in which students engaged in daily one-hour sessions focused on writing skills, authenticity in writing, proper prompting, and effective written expression. Students completed pre-test and post-test essay tasks, specifically reaction papers based on the Filipino film Heneral Luna. Their writing was scored using a standardized analytic rubric adapted from the MELAB writing assessment, covering content development, organization, vocabulary, structure/grammar, coherence, and mechanics. The study used a one-group pre-test/post-test quasi-experimental design and analyzed results with means, paired-sample t-tests, and Cohen's d effect sizes.

The participants were 32 Grade 11 students at UM Peñaplata College in the Philippines during school year 2024–2025, including 18 HUMSS and 14 ABM students. The study was conducted in a single institutional setting and included oversight from teachers and a licensed language teacher who validated scoring. The implementation emphasized monitored use of ChatGPT, including guidance against directly copying AI output and supervision during assessment conditions.

The main conclusion is that ChatGPT was associated with substantial improvement in students’ academic writing performance. Mean scores increased from 61.97 (SD = 14.36) on the pre-test to 84.69 (SD = 6.52) on the post-test, with a statistically significant gain, t(31) = 7.94, p < .05, and a large effect size (d = 1.40). Significant improvements were also reported across all rubric dimensions, with especially strong effects for coherence, content development, vocabulary, grammar, and organization. The authors conclude that ChatGPT can serve as an effective instructional support tool for academic writing when used with structure and guidance.
quality_tier_rationale: Peer-reviewed journal study using a quasi-experimental one-group pretest-posttest design with clear measures and reported inferential statistics, but no control/comparison group and substantial internal-validity limitations. This fits a well-described QED with important credibility concerns.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported effect on academic writing is large (Cohen’s d=1.40 overall, with large effects across most rubric dimensions), indicating strong positive impact in this sample of senior high school students, though estimates may be inflated by the uncontrolled design.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT was used as an AI-assisted academic writing support tool for Grade 11 students during a 14-day intervention to help them draft and improve reaction-paper writing, with emphasis on prompting, feedback use, paraphrasing rather than copying, and improving content, organization, vocabulary, grammar, coherence, and mechanics.

finding.finding_summary: This paper reports significant gains in Grade 11 students’ academic writing after a 14-day ChatGPT-supported intervention. In a one-group pretest-posttest sample of 32 students, overall writing scores increased from M=61.97 (SD=14.36) to M=84.69 (SD=6.52), t(31)=7.94, p<.05, with a large reported effect size of Cohen’s d=1.40 and 95% CI for the mean difference [16.882, 28.555]. Analytic rubric subscores also improved significantly: content development d=1.28, organization d=1.21, vocabulary d=1.28, structure/grammar d=1.25, coherence d=1.40, and mechanics d=0.93.
finding.measure: Reaction-paper essay writing quality scored with a modified MELAB analytic rubric assessing content development, organization, vocabulary, structure/grammar, coherence, and mechanics
finding.confidence_interval: 95% CI for mean difference overall = [16.882, 28.555]; subcomponent CIs reported in table
